library.description: PostgreSQL storage backend with native transactions and optional pgvector

blocks.text: English
把 PostgreSQL 接到统一存储接口，避免文本、记录、过期时间和应用 SQL 分别提交时出现一半更新成功的情况。将已有客户端或连接池交给对应驱动，再把插件安装到 host，就能在同一数据库事务中组合这些操作；通知、逻辑复制和向量等能力按需选择，客户端仍由应用负责关闭。

按需选择数据库功能。 COPY、通知、向量与可重放变更流分别导入，不选就不增加对应 API，见导入数据并发送通知。
能分清通知丢失和历史丢失。 普通通知不保证重放；逻辑复制提供检查点，并拒绝无法证明连续的历史，见持续读取变更。

组织共享物理表，同名键、期限、锁及标准向量点隔离。原生 SQL、自有向量表查询和 COPY 属于调用方表访问；显式组织视图拒绝这些入口。详细类型、并发、错误和日志限制见 USEGUIDE。
逻辑复制的 `truncate` 默认 `reset`。根流遇到 TRUNCATE 后，每个提交只发一条无 `orgId` 的 `reset`，消费者必须让所有组织缓存失效；`block` 会停止且不确认该提交。检测报告延迟与 WAL 保留量；无限 WAL 保留会警告。没有持续流需求时，不要保留复制 slot，可使用 TTL 或定时同步；关闭 host 不会删除 slot。

逻辑复制推荐仅发布当前 storage 的业务表（`kv`、`bytes`、`records` 及实际使用的向量表），并启用 insert/update/delete/truncate。显式表、专属 schema 和 `FOR ALL TABLES` publication 均可；原有全部表部署无需迁移。建表顺序、示例 SQL 和旧行为迁移见 持续读取变更。publication 缩小只减少输出和网络量，不减少整个数据库的 WAL 解码工作。

blocks.text: 这里写入一个固定组织。预期输出为 `ready`、`true`。
组织 ID 是 UUID 字符串。同名逻辑键、期限、锁和修订分别隔离；默认组织与其它组织共用物理表。`host.dropOrg(id)` 删除该组织的托管行，不删除其它组织或应用表。显式组织视图不允许任意 SQL、COPY 或自有向量表检索。
`getMany` 保留顺序、重复位置，缺失位置为 `undefined`。等价重复写键在 I/O 前拒绝。空批不做原生操作，也不调用 pipeline/hooks。省略 `ttlMs` 时保留活值的期限，新值没有期限；零立即过期。期限和锁使用数据库时钟。`counter.increment` 只接受规范十进制文本与安全整数，在写入前拒绝溢出。
默认根视图可使用 `store.sql`、`tx.sql` 访问应用表。插值是绑定参数；标识符使用 `@migaia/storage-host/sdk` 的 `sqlFragment.id`。同一事务可以混用应用 SQL 与标准存储方法。应用表的租户过滤由调用方提供。记录字段查询在客户端求值，原生规范键范围限制扫描。
事务请求 READ COMMITTED，检测会报告实际隔离级别。40001/40P01 经确认回滚后可能重试：观察到的修订没变时内部重放，变了才进入所选冲突策略。回调可能再次执行，外部副作用没有恰好一次保证。COMMIT 发出后连接中断不会盲目重放；提交标记可证明已提交，查不到或读失败都不能证明零写入。
先配置 `vector` 扩展。这里还选择 `halfvec` 量化召回，必要时会准备表达式索引；数据库与扩展版本必须支持它。输出取决于实际 ANN 候选，不承诺命中数量。

新建集合需要 `dimensions` 和 `metric`。metric 为 `cosine`、`dot`、`euclid`，分数分别为 `1-distance`、`-distance`、`-distance`。原向量存为 FLOAT32。`near(query, { exact: true })` 只对当前读取禁用 ANN；显式接 `rescore` 则选择量化召回。没有 `rescore` 时使用数据库现有计划和索引，单选 pgvector 不创建 ANN 索引。
量化模式在安装时选 `halfvec` 或 `binary_quantize`。`topK(k)` 限定候选数，`rescore({ topN })` 按原向量精确重排这些候选。topN 默认 k，必须是正安全整数且不超过 k。结果可以选字段、分组、通用 rerank，但不能删除、监听或再次 rescore，也不会隐式补读向量。
组织、期限及可下推 payload 条件进入原生召回过滤。ANN 过滤不保证最终足 k 条。JS 谓词仅过滤实际命中，不补搜；`requirePushdown()` 在 I/O 前拒绝需要客户端求值的条件。量化可能损失精度或发生原生转换错误。halfvec 索引最多4000维，binary 索引最多64000维，但原 vector 列最多16000维；这是上限，不是推荐配置。
同 schema/prefix/name 的集合配置跨组织、host 共享。dropOrg 保留配置和表结构。托管 `deleteWhere` 返回实际删除行数，包括物理尚在的过期匹配点。独立的 `api.pgvector.search` 接受结构化自有表目标和原生计划选项，不会把应用表变成托管集合。
示例创建应用表，导入两行 CSV，并把存储状态与通知放在同一次提交中。连接正常收到通知时预期输出 `done`；LISTEN 断线期间可能丢通知。

COPY 使用结构化表名、列名和返回异步字节流的 source factory。每次真实尝试重新调用 factory，不要传已消费的流。CSV 默认逗号、`header: false`；text 默认 TAB，支持省略 header 或显式 header:false；header:true 会拒绝。服务器文件和 PROGRAM 不支持。失败时先排空原生 COPY，再回滚。事务有 notify 和 COPY，没有 listen。
通知 channel 为非空 UTF-8 名，最多63字节；payload 少于8000字节，两者均拒绝 NUL。listen 返回订阅资源，需要释放。通知只是变化提示，不能证明断线消费者收到了所有提交。

部署方先配置 `wal_level=logical`、REPLICATION 角色与持久 pgoutput slot。publication 必须覆盖当前 schema/prefix 的 `kv`、`bytes`、`records` 表，以及 feed 使用的已创建向量表，并启用 `insert,update,delete,truncate`。`truncate: 'block'` 也需要发布 truncate，才能发现并停止该提交。把已有名称放入 `PG_REPLICATION_SLOT`、`PG_PUBLICATION`。该功能仅支持 PostgreSQL preset 的 `/pg` 驱动，检测不创建这些部署资源。
推荐先用相同 schema/prefix 安装不带复制 Feature 的后端以准备 storage 表，再由部署方创建仅包含所需表的 publication。默认 `public` / `migaia` 布局示例：

使用托管向量集合时，在下一次读取前用 `ALTER PUBLICATION ... ADD TABLE ...` 加入新建的向量物理表。也可把 storage 放在专属 schema，例如 `storage`，在该 schema 创建后用 `CREATE PUBLICATION migaia_storage_publication FOR TABLES IN SCHEMA storage WITH (publish = 'insert, update, delete, truncate');` 自动包含之后创建的表。专属 schema 只放需要发布的 storage 表；schema publication 也会发布该 schema 的其他合格表。

准入与迁移： 旧版本仅接受 `FOR ALL TABLES`；现在统一通过 `pg_publication_tables` 接受显式表、schema 与全部表三种 publication，只要覆盖 feed 的实际表和四种操作。原有启用全部操作的 `FOR ALL TABLES` 部署无需修改。缺表或关闭操作现在以 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` 拒绝，并在错误文本中指出表或操作；修正部署后重新检测。旧版本可能接受但不完整发布操作的配置，现在必须补齐四种操作。
PG16 逻辑解码文档说明逻辑 slot 对应一个数据库的变更流；publication 文档定义发布表与操作范围。逻辑解码仍读取整个数据库的 WAL，publication 只筛选 pgoutput 的输出表。缩小 publication 能减少无关变更的输出和网络量，不会把无关表的变更发给消费者，但不减少 WAL 解码本身的工作，也不能隔离同库 DDL 或保证消除解码错误。
使用已有 slot 时，PostgreSQL 可能需要先读取保留的旧 WAL，tailChanges 才能完成启动，示例随后的写入也会等待。启动耗时取决于积压，请先检查 confirmedFlushLagBytes 和 retainedWalBytes；不要为运行示例重置或共用生产 slot。
示例从当前进度开始，清理应用缓存并把已处理失效信息追加到文件。文件追加失败会使回调拒绝。没有 orgId 的 reset 必须处理为全组织失效。
`truncate` 默认 `reset`。根流每个 TRUNCATE 提交只发一条无 orgId 的 `kind: 'reset'`，需要清除全部组织缓存；组织流得到该组织自己的 reset。其它无 orgId 的非 reset 事件不能自动当全局事件。选择 `truncate: 'block'` 时停止、报告且不确认该提交。

`onChange` 成功才允许确认；回调拒绝就停止，不确认该提交。轮询 `readChanges({ after, limit })` 返回 `{ changes, cursor }`。先完成派生写入，再保存 cursor，下次把已保存 cursor 传回 after，才确认完整进度。游标可能包含部分提交进度，不要解析、修改或自行加减位置。slot 丢失或历史不再可证明连续时抛 `CHANGE_CURSOR_EXPIRED`，一个 slot 只允许一个活跃消费者。

`onCapabilityProbe` 带出十进制字符串 `confirmedFlushLagBytes`（当前 WAL 位置减已确认位置）、`retainedWalBytes`（当前位置减 slot restart 位置）及 `maxSlotWalKeepSize`。无限保留值 `-1` 经 reporter 发出警告，不使检测失败，也不修改服务端设置。延迟和保留量都要关注，断开的 slot 可能持续占用磁盘。
释放 tail 或 host 只结束复制连接，不关闭 pool、不删除 slot/publication。没有持续流需求时不要保留 slot，可用 TTL 或定时同步。删 slot 是单独的管理操作；`api.logicalReplication.dropSlot()` 存在，但不是默认清理步骤。
宿主默认自动检测。设置 autoDetect:false 后，使用所选功能前应先 await host.detect()；托管向量首次实际使用仍会检查扩展。

items: 默认 `server: 'postgres'`、schema `public`、prefix `migaia`；driver 必填。`maxLockMs` 默认60000ms并限定租约，`concurrency` 选择冲突策略。cockroach、yugabyte 需要实际服务检测；协议连接成功不等于 PostgreSQL 专属功能可用。
`/pg` 借用 Pool，`/postgres-js` 借用 postgres.Sql，`/bun` 借用 Bun 1.4.4+ 且 prepare:false 的 SQL。先结束 host，再关闭相应客户端。根入口不加载驱动；复制额外需要 Node 22+ 及声明的复制 peer。能力检查不表示每个服务和运行时组合都已实际验收。
文本、记录使用支持 Map/Set 的便携集合编码，字节复制。记录键用规范保序字节，其它通道用同一身份的 hex。文本/字节缺失为 null，记录/metadata 缺失为 undefined。私有表不能当应用 SQL 接口；JSONB payload 只是过滤投影。
SQL 的 int8 返回 bigint，numeric/date/JSON/array 保留原生文本，bytea 返回独立 Uint8Array。不安装全局 parser。postgres.js 字符串参数使用 TEXT，需要其它类型时由应用 SQL 显式转换。
本包错误 source 为 storage.backend.postgres，码为 SQL_FAILED、DECODE_FAILED、TRANSACTION_FAILED、DUPLICATE_KEY。校验、取消、期限和并发错误保留各自 source；原错误可沿 cause 或 aggregate errors 找到。观察回调错误只报告；要改变操作，请用 pipeline。
用 `@migaia/storage-host/plugins/journal` 的 `storageJournalPlugin(options)` 显式启用日志。text/bytes/record/托管 vector 的完整镜像及绝对期限在数据事务内捕获；外置 binlog 在提交后追加并等待完成，失败只报告，不能撤回数据。完整镜像模式在执行前拒绝原生 SQL、COPY、自有向量表终点。
原生日志在每个数据库事务内串行更新 head/record，不跨操作缓存索引。外置 WAL 先写 intent，再随数据写独立 marker，重开时区分已提交和未完成修改。undo 仅在宿主支持的日志组合中出现，先锁定全部目标并核对完整修订和镜像，再恢复；组织重建不让旧镜像重新有效，缺少 birth 的旧镜像以 UNDO_CONFLICT 拒绝，不能跨组织恢复。
日志按执行顺序保留重复写和中间值。undo 核对最终修订、恢复原绝对期限，不刷新已过期期限。telemetry 独立启用，每个根操作或完整事务跨重试只发一条完成事件，不接管 logger；先释放 host，再释放 logger 及其载体。

Use PostgreSQL through one storage API when text, records, expiry and application SQL must commit together rather than leave half an update saved. Pass an existing client or pool to its driver and install the plugin in a host, then combine these operations in the same database transaction. Select notifications, logical replication or vectors separately when needed; your application still closes the client.

items: The order row exists but its status does not: the two writes committed separately.
A rebuilt cache still serves stale data: a notification channel was treated as replayable history.
Two tenants overwrite the same key: tenant filtering varies between queries.
Shutdown hangs: the client pool closes before subscriptions and storage work have finished.
Commit storage operations and SQL together. KV, records and SQL in a transaction use the same connection. See Transactions and organizations.
Add only the database features you need. COPY, notifications, vectors and replayable changes have separate imports and explicit selection. See Import and notify.
Know when history is no longer safe to resume. Notifications may be lost; logical replication supplies checkpoints and rejects unprovable gaps. See Follow committed changes.
Keep batch semantics clear. Reads retain input order and duplicates, while writes reject equivalent duplicate keys. Array parameters avoid issuing one query per key; no speed comparison is claimed.

blocks.text: Defaults are `server: 'postgres'`, `schema: 'public'` and `prefix: 'migaia'`. `cockroach` and `yugabyte` require actual server detection. Only PostgreSQL provides the ordinary change notifications; Cockroach does not support this module's pgvector Feature. Wire compatibility does not verify every deployment combination.

Organizations share tables while isolating equal keys, expiry, locks and standard vector points. Raw SQL, caller-table vector search and COPY access application tables; explicit organization views reject those endpoints. See Behavior and limits for data types, concurrency, failures and journal restrictions.

Logical replication defaults to `truncate: 'reset'`. Root streams emit one reset without `orgId` per TRUNCATE commit: consumers must invalidate every organization. `block` stops without confirming that commit. Detection reports replication lag and retained WAL and warns about unlimited retention. Keep no replication slot when a live stream is unnecessary; TTL or periodic synchronization may suffice. Host disposal never removes a slot.

For logical replication, publish only the current storage business tables (`kv`, `bytes`, `records` and any vector tables in use), with insert/update/delete/truncate enabled. Explicit-table, dedicated-schema and `FOR ALL TABLES` publications are accepted; existing all-table deployments need no migration. See Follow committed changes for table preparation, SQL and migration details. Narrower publications reduce output and network traffic, not WAL decoding for the whole database.

blocks.text: This writes into one fixed organization. Expected output is `ready` followed by `true`.

Organizations use UUID strings. Equal logical keys, TTL, locks and revisions remain separate; the default organization shares the physical tables. `host.dropOrg(id)` removes that organization's managed rows, not other organizations or application tables. Organization views reject raw SQL, COPY and caller-table vector search.

`getMany` keeps order, duplicates and `undefined` for missing positions. Equivalent duplicate write keys reject before I/O. Empty batches perform no native operation or pipeline/hook work. Omitted `ttlMs` preserves a live deadline; a new value has no deadline. Zero expires immediately. TTL and locks use the database clock. `counter.increment` works on canonical decimal text and rejects unsafe integers before writing.

Use `store.sql` or `tx.sql` on the default root for application tables. Interpolated values are parameters, not SQL source; use `sqlFragment.id` from `@migaia/storage-host/sdk` for identifiers. A root transaction may mix application SQL and standard storage methods. Supply your own tenant filters for application tables. Record query fields are evaluated by the shared client-side query code; native key ranges bound the scan.

Transactions request READ COMMITTED, and detection reports the actual isolation level. SQLSTATE 40001/40P01 can trigger replay after a confirmed rollback: unchanged observed revisions permit internal retry; changed revisions enter the selected concurrency policy. Callbacks may run again. Do not rely on exactly-once external effects. After COMMIT was sent, a connection failure never triggers blind replay. A transaction marker can prove commit; missing or unreadable evidence cannot prove no write occurred.

Provision the `vector` extension before selecting this Feature. The example also selects `halfvec` quantized recall and creates its expression index when needed; the database version and extension must support it. Its output depends on actual ANN candidates, rather than a promised result count.

`dimensions` and `metric` are required when creating a collection. Metrics are `cosine`, `dot` and `euclid`; scores are respectively `1-distance`, `-distance` and `-distance`. Points store FLOAT32 vectors. `near(query, { exact: true })` disables ANN for that read unless an explicit `rescore` stage selects quantized recall. Without `rescore`, existing database indexes and plans are used; plain pgvector selection does not create ANN indexes.

Quantization selects `halfvec` or `binary_quantize` once during installation. `topK(k)` bounds recall; `rescore({ topN })` reorders those candidates using original vectors. `topN` defaults to k and must be a positive safe integer no larger than k. Rescored queries can select fields, group and use generic rerank; they cannot delete, watch or rescore twice. No extra vector fetch is implied.

Organization, expiry and supported payload conditions appear in the native recall filter. ANN filtering does not guarantee k surviving hits. JavaScript predicates filter returned hits without refill. `requirePushdown()` rejects conditions that need client evaluation before I/O. Quantization may lose precision or reject native casts. Halfvec indexes allow up to 4000 dimensions; binary indexes up to 64000, while the original vector column allows up to 16000. These are limits, not recommended dimensions.

Collection configuration is shared across organizations and hosts using the same schema/prefix/name. `dropOrg` retains that configuration and table structure. Managed `deleteWhere` returns actual deleted rows, including expired matches that still physically exist. The separate `api.pgvector.search` accepts a structured caller-table target and native planner options; it does not turn application tables into managed collections.

The program creates an application table, imports two CSV rows and commits a storage status with the notification. Expected output is `done` when the connected listener receives the committed notification. LISTEN is a live channel and can be lost on disconnect.

COPY accepts structured table/column names and a source factory returning an async byte iterable. Each actual attempt calls the factory again; never pass a consumed stream. CSV defaults to comma and `header: false`. Text defaults to TAB. Omitted header and explicit header:false are supported; header:true rejects. Server files and PROGRAM are unsupported. On failure, native COPY drains before rollback. Transactions expose notify and COPY, but no listen method.

Notification channels are nonempty UTF-8 names of at most 63 bytes; payloads are below 8000 bytes. Neither accepts NUL. `listen` returns a subscription that must be disposed. Notifications are hints, not durable delivery or proof that a disconnected consumer saw every commit.

Prepare `wal_level=logical`, a REPLICATION role and a persistent pgoutput slot. The publication must include the selected schema/prefix's `kv`, `bytes` and `records` tables, plus existing vector tables consumed by the feed, and enable `insert,update,delete,truncate`. The `truncate: 'block'` policy also needs truncate publication to detect and stop that commit. Set `PG_REPLICATION_SLOT` and `PG_PUBLICATION` to their existing names. Only the PostgreSQL preset with `/pg` supports this Feature. Detection checks those facts without creating deployment resources.

First install the backend without the replication Feature using the same schema/prefix to prepare its storage tables. Then have deployment create a publication containing only the required tables. For the default `public` / `migaia` layout:

When using managed vector collections, add each new physical vector table with `ALTER PUBLICATION ... ADD TABLE ...` before the next feed read. Alternatively, keep storage in a dedicated schema such as `storage`. After creating that schema, `CREATE PUBLICATION migaia_storage_publication FOR TABLES IN SCHEMA storage WITH (publish = 'insert, update, delete, truncate');` also includes future tables. Keep that schema limited to the storage tables you intend to publish; a schema publication includes its other eligible tables too.

Admission and migration: older versions accepted only `FOR ALL TABLES`. Admission now uses `pg_publication_tables` uniformly for explicit-table, schema-wide and all-table publications covering every feed table and all four operations. Existing `FOR ALL TABLES` deployments with all operations enabled need no change. Missing tables or disabled operations raise `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` with the missing table or operation in the message; repair deployment and detect again. Previously accepted configurations that omitted operation types must enable all four.

The PG16 logical decoding documentation describes a logical slot as one database's change stream; publications select the tables and operations to publish. Logical decoding still reads WAL for the whole database. A publication filters pgoutput's output tables. Narrowing it reduces unrelated output and network traffic and keeps unrelated table changes out of the consumer stream, but does not reduce WAL decoding itself, isolate concurrent DDL in the same database or guarantee that decoding errors disappear.

With an existing slot, PostgreSQL may need to read retained older WAL before tailChanges finishes starting, so the next write in this example also waits. Startup time depends on that backlog: inspect confirmedFlushLagBytes and retainedWalBytes first, and do not reset or share a production slot to run this example.

This example starts at the current position, invalidates application caches and appends each processed invalidation to a file. A failed append rejects the callback. It also shows the required handling of a reset that has no organization.

`truncate` defaults to `reset`. A root TRUNCATE produces exactly one `kind: 'reset'` without `orgId` for its commit; invalidate every organization's cached data. A routed organization feed gets its organization's reset. Do not treat every untagged non-reset event as a global event. With `truncate: 'block'`, the consumer stops, reports the condition and does not confirm the commit.

A successful `onChange` permits acknowledgement; rejection stops the stream without confirming that commit. For polling, `readChanges({ after, limit })` returns `{ changes, cursor }`. Commit derived effects and save `cursor` only after processing succeeds; pass that saved cursor as the next `after` to confirm completed progress. Cursors include complete or partial commit progress, so never parse, edit or advance them manually. Lost slots or expired/unprovable history raise `CHANGE_CURSOR_EXPIRED`. One slot supports one active consumer.

`onCapabilityProbe` includes decimal-string `confirmedFlushLagBytes` (current WAL position minus confirmed progress) and `retainedWalBytes` (current WAL position minus the slot's restart position), plus `maxSlotWalKeepSize`. Unlimited retention (`-1`) sends a warning through the reporter; it does not fail detection or change server settings. Monitor both lag and retained WAL, because a disconnected slot can retain disk indefinitely.

Disposing the tail or host releases replication connections and leaves the pool, slot and publication intact. Keep no slot when a live stream is unnecessary; TTL or periodic synchronization can avoid that retained-WAL obligation. Slot removal is a separate intentional administrative action; `api.logicalReplication.dropSlot()` exists but is not a cleanup default.

Host detection runs automatically by default. If you set autoDetect:false, call await host.detect() before relying on the selected features. Managed vector endpoints still check the extension at first real use.

items: Defaults: `server: 'postgres'`, schema `public`, prefix `migaia`; `driver` is required. `maxLockMs` defaults to 60000 ms and bounds their lease, and `concurrency` selects conflict handling. `cockroach` and `yugabyte` require their actual detected server behavior; PostgreSQL-only features do not become available merely because the wire protocol connects.

Drivers: `/pg` borrows `Pool`; `/postgres-js` borrows `postgres.Sql`; `/bun` borrows Bun 1.4.4+ `SQL` configured with `prepare: false`. Close each SDK only after host release. The root imports none of them. Logical replication additionally uses Node 22+ and its declared `pg-logical-replication` peer. Server compatibility and adapter capability checks are not a promise that every runtime/server combination has been exercised.

Data: text/records use portable collection-aware codecs, including Map/Set. Bytes are copied. Record keys use canonical ordered bytes; other channels encode the same key identity as hex. Missing text/bytes return `null`; records/metadata return `undefined`. Private storage tables are not an application SQL API. JSONB payload columns support filters, not a different truth value.

SQL results: int8 is bigint; numeric/date/JSON/array retain native text; bytea becomes independent Uint8Array. No global parser is installed. postgres.js string parameters use TEXT; cast values explicitly in application SQL when another database type is required.

Errors: module failures use source `storage.backend.postgres` and `SQL_FAILED`, `DECODE_FAILED`, `TRANSACTION_FAILED` or `DUPLICATE_KEY`. Shared validation, cancellation, timeout and concurrency codes keep their own source. Original errors remain reachable through `cause` or aggregate `errors`. Observer failures are reported; use pipelines to change an operation.

Journals are opt-in through `storageJournalPlugin(options)` from `@migaia/storage-host/plugins/journal`. Full text/bytes/record/managed-vector images and absolute expiry are captured in the data transaction. External binlog append happens after commit and is awaited; append failure reports but cannot roll back committed data. Full-image logging rejects raw SQL, COPY and caller-table vector endpoints before executing them.

Native log storage serializes head/record updates in each database transaction and does not cache an index between operations. External WAL writes intent first and a separate marker with the data; recovery distinguishes committed data from unfinished intent. Undo is available only for the supported host journal combination, locks every target and verifies complete revisions/images before restoring. Recreating an organization cannot make old undo images valid; old images without revision birth reject with `UNDO_CONFLICT`. Cross-organization restoration is not allowed.

Selected logs preserve repeated writes and intermediate values in execution order. Undo compares the final revision and restores original absolute deadlines; an expired deadline is not extended. Telemetry is separately opt-in, reports one completed root operation/transaction across retries and never takes ownership of the logger. Release the logger and its storage only after the host.
